From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Ops sprint sizing — burst windows & GPU selection

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and the information we need to lock a dedicated-capacity proposal: 

1) Traffic shape / burst windows: you mentioned 1,200 TPS sustained during business hours with 3 short burst windows (5–8 minutes) where TPS spikes to ~6,000 for alerting/ingestion. Please confirm the weekday distribution (Mon–Fri) vs weekend behavior and whether bursts are predictable (cron-like) or event-driven.

2) Token mix & latency SLOs: current prompt+response average token count is ~950 tokens (prompts ~200 / responses ~750). Target 95th latency SLO is 350ms for single-request flows; background async jobs can tolerate ~800ms. Confirm if these numbers look right.

3) Concurrency and KV cache behavior: do you expect many long-lived streaming sessions (chat-style) or mostly short inference calls? If streaming, what's the typical max concurrent sessions?

4) Deployment mode preference: you said security is important and you are evaluating Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPU pool) vs Private VPC. For the initial POC, do you want us to size for Dedicated and provide a VPC parity estimate, or go straight to a VPC sizing?

5) GPU family preference: any constraints (NVIDIA A100 vs H100 vs lower-cost T4/RTX for quantized models)? If you have existing on-prem hardware we should match to, please share model-profile_samples.csv (attached) or the AMI/instance names.

Next steps: if you can confirm items 1–3 and attach a short sample traffic CSV (15–30 days of minute-level TPS) we'll run a micro-benchmark and return two sizing options: (A) low-latency Dedicated pool (SLA-backed) and (B) cost-optimized Dedicated with burst autoscaling.

I've attached a starter capacity runbook and the small model profile you referenced. Proposed micro-benchmark window: 48 hours after we receive the CSV.

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Ops sprint sizing — burst windows & GPU selection

Jordan — thanks for the concise recap. Confirming the numbers below and adding context: 

- Traffic shape: 1,200 TPS baseline Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 PT. Three predictable bursts tied to batch ingests at 09:15, 12:30 and 16:45 local — each lasts roughly 6–9 minutes. Weekend traffic drops to ~200 TPS with no bursts.
- Token mix: your prompt/response split is accurate; occasional longer responses (1,500 tokens) for some admin-reporting endpoints (~3% of requests).
- Concurrency: mostly short calls. We do have ~350 long-lived streaming sessions for analyst chat during work hours, but those are low-rate per-session.

We are leaning Dedicated for the POC to validate latency SLAs quickly; security team will want a VPC estimate as follow-up. We do not have on-prem GPUs to match.

For GPU family, preferred would be H100 if its latency profile maps to our 95th SLO, but we are sensitive to cost — happy to see both H100 and A100 recommendations.

I'll push the minute-level CSV to the shared drive link in the HubSpot task by EOD. Procurement copied for contract/po timeline.

—Alex

Thanks Alex — that's super helpful. A few notes from the sizing/infra side based on what you shared: 

- Baseline 1,200 TPS + predictable ~6–9 minute spikes to 6k TPS implies we should design for two operating points: sustained pool for baseline + short-duration burst capacity. For Dedicated we typically recommend a mix of H100-backed instances for tail-sensitive routes and a pool of quantized A10/A30-style instances for throughput-heavy, less latency-sensitive endpoints.
- Given the token mix (95th latency target 350ms) and occasional 1.5k token responses, H100 instances (or A100-80GB where available) are the safest baseline to meet the SLO. We'll provide an A/B cost tradeoff (H100-primary vs A100-primary with quantization).
- For streaming sessions: plan for ~350 concurrent long-lived sessions; we should reserve a small portion of KV-cache-friendly capacity (persistent VMs) rather than fully multiplexing on the burst pool to avoid cache thrashing.

Action items for us (internal):
1) Jordan to collect the minute-level CSV from Alex and upload to the sizing pipeline.
2) Marissa to run the micro-benchmark once CSV is available; expected 48-hour run.
3) Ben to prepare a quick pricing sketch (H100 vs A100) + procurement notes for PO lead time.

Ben/Marissa — any concerns with the above approach? I'll draft the Dedicated sizing options once the CSV lands.

Thanks — Karthik
